If the wrapped call ever fails, the failure is silently swallowed and there's no way to diagnose what went wrong.

File: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/result_consumer.py, Line: 131, Issue: Eager thread spawn: In `__init__`, `FixedQueuePool` is constructed immediately when the factory is created in `thread-queue-parallel` mode, which spawns `max_workers or 20` daemon worker threads at construction time. Unlike the other modes (where the `ThreadPoolExecutor`/`MultiprocessingPool` work is tied to strategy creation), merely instantiating the factory — e.g., for CLI validation or in code paths that never call `create_with_partitions` — now costs 20 live threads. Also note `max_workers or 20` silently substitutes 20 when `max_workers` is None or 0, which differs from the "max workers" semantics of the other parallel modes; consider making the default explicit or validating the value.

File: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/result_consumer.py, Line: 182, Issue: Shutdown leaves dangling strategy: `shutdown()` shuts down the pool and sets `self.queue_pool = None`, but any `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` previously returned by `create_with_partitions` still holds a reference to that pool and keeps its commit thread running. If the strategy's `submit()` is invoked after `shutdown()` (e.g., in-flight messages during teardown, as the graceful-shutdown test exercises), `assert self.queue_pool is not None` in `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` has already passed, but the strategy will keep submitting into a shut-down pool whose queues raise `queue.ShutDown`; the resulting exception path marks offsets complete without processing them, so those messages can be committed as done despite never being handled. Consider having the factory coordinate strategy shutdown, or make the strategy resilient to a shut-down pool.

File: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py, Line: 148, Issue: Data loss on processing errors: In `OrderedQueueWorker.run`, if `result_processor` raises, the exception is logged and the offset is marked complete in the `finally` block. The message is then effectively dropped: `OffsetTracker` will consider it processed and the commit loop will commit past it, so the message is never retried. This silently converts an at-least-once consumer into at-most-once for any transient error (e.g., a DB timeout while handling an uptime result). If the failed item is the highest offset in the partition, the offset is committed on the next commit cycle and the data is permanently lost. Consider leaving the offset outstanding on failure, or routing failures to a retry/dead-letter path.

File: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py, Line: 297, Issue: Failed decodes silently dropped: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`, the `except Exception` handler marks the failing message's offset as added and completed, so a message that fails to decode or group is skipped and its offset becomes committable. Combined with the commit loop, this means malformed/unexpected payloads are permanently dropped with only a log line. If dropping is intentional for poison messages, it should be explicit (e.g., a dedicated metric/counter and comment); otherwise the offset should not be completed so the message is retried.

File: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py, Line: 84, Issue: Performance: offset scan cost: `get_committable_offsets` iterates `range(start, max_offset + 1)` while holding the partition lock. If a partition has a large gap between `last_committed`/`min_offset` and `max_offset` (e.g., a compacted topic or large offset jump after a seek), this loop runs once per second per partition over potentially millions of offsets, blocking `add_offset`/`complete_offset` for that partition. A sorted structure or heap per partition would avoid the linear scan.

File: tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py, Line: 118, Issue: Flaky assertion: `test_different_groups_distributed` asserts that 20 group keys hash to exactly 3 distinct queue indices. The assignment uses Python's `hash(group_key) % num_queues`, which is not guaranteed to cover all 3 queues for an arbitrary set of 20 keys (and string hashing is randomized per process unless PYTHONHASHSEED is fixed). On some runs only 1 or 2 queues will be hit, making this test intermittently fail. A weaker assertion (e.g., `1 <= len(queue_indices) <= 3`, or checking distribution over many more keys) would be deterministic.

File: tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py, Line: 216, Issue: Race condition in test: In `test_stats_reporting`, the assertion `stats["total_items"] > 0` is made immediately after submitting 10 items, but worker threads may have already drained the queues before `get_stats()` is called, making `total_items` 0 and failing the assertion. File: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py, Line: 1830, Issue: Test contradicts implementation: `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` asserts that no offsets are committed when processing fails (`len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`). The test should either assert that the failed offset is still committed (matching actual behavior) or the implementation should not complete offsets for failed messages.

findings: File: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, Line: 1022, Issue: Possible Bug: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is called with an empty `data` object. Prisma's `updateMany` with an empty data payload can raise a validation error, and even if accepted, it relies entirely on Prisma's `@updatedAt` side effect to bump `updatedAt` — the comment says the intent is to update `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, but no field is actually passed. If `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not annotated with `@updatedAt` (this PR only adds that annotation to `CalendarCache`), the call updates nothing and the cache-status feature silently shows stale data. Passing an explicit field (e.g. a last-synced timestamp) would make the intent robust.

File: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, Line: 1022, Issue: Unconditional write on read path: The update runs on every invocation of this method, touching all `SelectedCalendar` rows for the credential even when the availability fetch was served from a fresh cache or only one calendar's data changed. This adds a DB write per availability check (a hot path during booking flows) and makes `updatedAt` reflect "any fetch happened" rather than a meaningful per-calendar sync time, weakening the cache-status signal this PR introduces.

File: apps/web/package.json, Line: 11, Issue: Dependency resolution: The `dev:cron` script now uses `npx tsx` instead of a package-manager-managed binary. If `tsx` is not declared as a devDependency of this workspace, `npx` will silently download and run it from the npm registry at invocation time, pinning no version and making the dev script depend on network access and whatever the latest `tsx` release is. Prefer adding `tsx` to devDependencies and invoking it directly (e.g., `yarn tsx cron-tester.ts`) so the version is locked and no implicit fetch occurs.

File: packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts, Line: 172, Issue: Expired cache reported as valid: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups `CalendarCache` rows by `credentialId` and returns only the max `updatedAt`, without filtering on `expiresAt`. Cache entries in this table carry an `expiresAt` field (visible in the schema), so a credential whose only cache rows are already expired will still be reported as having a valid cache with a recent `updatedAt`. The UI (CredentialActionsDropdown) uses this value to display "Cache Status / Last updated", so users will see a healthy cache status for credentials whose cached availability has actually expired. findings: File: packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx, Line: 47, Issue: Accessibility regression: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the password visibility toggle button removes it from keyboard tab order. Keyboard-only users can no longer toggle password visibility, which is an accessibility regression for a shared UI component used by all password fields (including the login and 2FA password inputs in this PR). If the intent was to prevent the toggle from stealing focus during form autofill/submission, a more targeted fix (e.g., `onMouseDown={e => e.preventDefault()}`) would preserve keyboard access.

File: apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx, Line: 21, Issue: Input validation gap: The `minLength={10}` / `maxLength={11}` constraints don't enforce the expected format. A 10-character value containing a dash (e.g. "1234-56789") passes HTML validation, but the server strips dashes before comparing (`replaceAll("-", "")`), so it becomes a 9-character string that can never match a stored 10-character code. Similarly, arbitrary non-code characters are accepted since there is no `pattern` check. Adding a pattern like `^[0-9a-f]{5}-?[0-9a-f]{5}$` (matching the hex codes generated server-side) would reject malformed input up front instead of producing a confusing "incorrect backup code" error.

File: apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx, Line: 21, Issue: Missing validation feedback: The field is marked `required` but no error message or `aria-invalid` handling is provided, and unlike the sibling `TwoFactor` component (which gained an `autoFocus` prop in this PR), this component offers no `autoFocus` option. When the user submits the login/disable forms with an empty backup code, browser-native validation text appears with no styled feedback consistent with the rest of the form, and keyboard users landing on the backup-code step must manually tab to the field.

File: apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx, Line: 21, Issue: Conflicting defaultValue: `defaultValue=""` is passed alongside `{...methods.register("backupCode")}`. In react-hook-form, the registered input's value is controlled by the form state; the explicit `defaultValue` prop is redundant and can conflict with `methods.setValue("backupCode", "")` reset calls made by the parent forms (login.tsx and DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx), depending on render timing. Dropping `defaultValue` (or using `defaultValues` in `useForm`) is the conventional pattern.

File: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts, Line: 61, Issue: Backup codes silently invalidated: Every call to the setup endpoint overwrites `backupCodes` with a freshly generated set. If a user who already has 2FA enabled (and previously saved backup codes) opens the setup flow again — or calls it repeatedly without completing enablement — their previously issued backup codes are destroyed and replaced, even if the user cancels the setup afterwards. A user relying on a saved backup code will find it rejected at login. Consider only generating backup codes when they don't already exist, or confirming before regenerating.

File: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts, Line: 55, Issue: Unhandled JSON.parse: `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...))` is called without a try/catch. If the stored `backupCodes` value is corrupted, was written by an older format, or decryption yields non-JSON output, this throws an unhandled exception and the client receives a raw 500 instead of a structured error. The sibling login flow in `next-auth-options.ts` has the same pattern, but here the failure also aborts the disable flow entirely. Wrap the parse/decrypt in try/catch and return a 400/500 JSON error.

File: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts, Line: 46, Issue: Unvalidated input type: `req.body.backupCode` is used directly in `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` without validating it is a string. A client posting `{"backupCode": 123}` or `{"backupCode": {"a": 1}}` (JSON bodies allow non-string values) causes `replaceAll` to throw a TypeError, resulting in an unhandled 500 rather than the intended `IncorrectBackupCode` 400 response. Add a `typeof req.body.backupCode === "string"` check.

File: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts, Line: 50, Issue: Untested assertion: The newly added FIXME documents that the existing `isChecked()` check on `two-factor-switch` passes even when the switch is not checked, yet the assertion is left in place and the underlying bug is not fixed in this PR. Since this helper is used to set up every 2FA test in the file, a regression that leaves 2FA disabled after setup could go undetected while later steps fail with confusing errors. Consider replacing it with the reliable `data-state="checked"` visibility check already used a few lines below.

File: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts, Line: 113, Issue: Missing assertions: The new backup-code steps include TODOs for verifying the downloaded file content and the clipboard content, so the test only asserts that a download named `cal-backup-codes.txt` occurs and that a success toast appears. A regression that downloads empty or wrong backup codes (e.g., a formatting bug in `formatBackupCode`) would pass this test. At minimum, reading the download stream and asserting it contains 10 codes in `XXXXX-XXXXX` format would close the gap.

File: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts, Line: 138, Issue: Unhandled JSON.parse: `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...))` is called without a try/catch. If the stored `backupCodes` value is corrupted, was encrypted with a different/rotated `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, or is otherwise not valid JSON, `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` will throw an unhandled exception inside `authorize`. This surfaces as an opaque NextAuth internal error instead of a user-facing message, and unlike the other failure paths (IncorrectBackupCode, MissingBackupCodes) the login page cannot map it to a helpful error. Wrapping the decrypt/parse in a try/catch and throwing `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` (or a dedicated error) would degrade gracefully.

File: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts, Line: 143, Issue: Backup code consumed on match only after password check - but no rate-limit distinction: The backup-code verification uses `backupCodes.indexOf(...)` (a plain string comparison) on secrets that are long-lived, reusable-until-used credentials. Unlike TOTP codes (30-second window), a backup code remains valid indefinitely, so an attacker who can repeatedly hit `authorize` with a password candidate can brute-force the 40-bit code space without any per-code expiry. If the existing rate limit earlier in `authorize` applies per-email/password and is not tightened for failed backup-code attempts, this is a weaker link than the TOTP path. Note: I cannot see the full rate-limiting configuration in this diff, so the actual exposure depends on limits defined elsewhere.

Conversely, if `backupCode` was added to the schema as required, the normal TOTP path would fail. Verify the schema allows exactly one of the two fields depending on the active mode. File: apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx, Line: 156, Issue: Stale State: When the server responds with `ErrorCode.SecondFactorRequired`, only `twoFactorRequired` is set to true; `twoFactorLostAccess` is never reset. If a user toggled "lost access", submitted a wrong backup code, then went all the way back and re-submitted credentials triggering 2FA again, the stale `twoFactorLostAccess` state could leave the form showing the backup-code input (or an inconsistent footer) instead of the TOTP input. Resetting `twoFactorLostAccess` alongside `setTwoFactorRequired(true)` would make the state deterministic.

File: apps/web/components/settings/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx, Line: 44, Issue: Stale validation errors: `resetForm` clears field values via `form.setValue` and the error message state, but does not call `form.clearErrors()` or `form.reset()`. File: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, Line: 163, Issue: State inconsistency on dialog close: At the `DisplayBackupCodes` step the cancel button is hidden and the only in-dialog exit is the "close" button, which calls `resetState()` and `onEnable()`. File: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, Line: 68, Issue: Incomplete state reset: `resetState()` clears the password, error, and step but not `backupCodes` or `backupCodesUrl`. The generated backup codes and their blob URL persist in component state after the flow completes. Since the modal is mounted per-open this is low severity, but if the component is reused the stale secret material lingers in memory and the object URL is never revoked on unmount.
